newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cargill to sign accord for Brazil sugar terminal.
newsitem.headline: Cargill to sign accord for Brazil sugar terminal.

text.p: Cargill Agricola, the Brazilian unit of Cargill Inc, is to sign Monday a pact with Santos port authority for a sugar terminal, a port spokesman said.
Cargill intends to build a terminal on a 70,000 square meter concession which will handle both bulk and bagged sugar, said the spokesman for the Codesp port authority.

The concession is to last 20 years. Under the terms of the agreement, the terminal will handle a minimum of 600,000 tonnes in the first two years of operation, 750,000 for the following two years and one million tonnes by the fifth year.
Investment is projected at 33.16 million reais (US$32.51 million) at least, of which 28.16 million reais will be made available in the project's first year, according to the pact.
At the latest, work should begin a month after Codesp approves the contract, and should be completed in 15 months.

Traders estimate the new terminal will not be operational at the earliest until the 1998/99 harvest in the center-south, which runs from May to November. Cargill already leases a bulk sugar terminal at Santos which traders said handles between 450,000 and 500,000 tonnes of sugar a year.
